I couldn't run the tests (Bash was denied), so this comes from reading the code only.

**Finding:** `src/router/escalation.ts:26` puts `context_overflow` in `SWITCH_IMMEDIATELY`. Line 53 then marks that provider dead at every tier, and line 64 leaves dead providers out of `tierUp`. So a brief that overflows the context can never move up to a higher tier on the same provider. When the provider is pinned (`candidates` holds only that provider, per `policy.ts:131`), the ladder stops right away with "ladder exhausted". That contradicts the comment at `delegate.ts:307`, which says a brief too large to start with "goes up the ladder".

**Do I agree?** Mostly yes, as a real bug in the pinned case. Whether it matters for unpinned runs depends on whether a provider's higher-tier model actually has a bigger context window. If it doesn't, switching providers is reasonable. Treating `rate_limited` as dead for the whole subtask is a smaller issue of the same kind.
